Memory-optimization pass across upload/import pipeline: queued single-file processing with pacing delay + gc.collect(), zip-bomb guard, explicit BS4/bytes release; self-corrected a duplicate library method added in error

Per direct instruction to review the whole app for memory optimization. Restructured assets_upload(): previously did hash+dedup-check+DB-register+thumbnail for every file back-to-back inside a single request; now the request only streams each file to disk (f.save(), unchanged, already memory-safe) and pushes a small job dict onto a new _asset_process_queue. A single serial background thread (_asset_worker) pulls one job at a time and does all the heavier work (chunked hash, dedup check against current DB state, add_record, thumbnail) for that one file only, then calls gc.collect() and sleeps 0.4s before picking up the next - so at any given moment at most one file's worth of processing memory is in use, never a whole batch's worth at once. The manifest fsync is still only performed once per drained batch (checked via _asset_process_queue.empty()), preserving the earlier per-batch-not-per-file fsync fix from pkg39/40 rather than regressing it back to per-file. Also added: explicit 'del raw' plus gc.collect() in api_import_process_item() right after HTML parsing, so the full file bytes and the BS4 parse tree are released immediately rather than waiting for Python's next automatic GC cycle; and a 300MB total-uncompressed-size guard on App-import ZIP extraction in app_new(), computed from the zip's central directory listing (z.infolist()) with no decompression required, rejecting oversized archives before extractall() runs - protects against a small zip expanding into something that exhausts memory or disk on a constrained device.
